en.21:33: Listen to another parable: There was a landowner who planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a winepress in it, and built a tower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.
en.21:34: When the harvest time drew near, he sent his servants to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit.
en.21:35: But the tenants seized his servants. They beat one, killed another, and stoned a third.
en.21:36: Again, he sent other servants, more than the first group. But the tenants did the same to them.
en.21:37: Finally, he sent his son to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.
en.21:38: But when the tenants saw the son, they said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and take his inheritance.’
en.21:39: So they seized him and threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.
en.21:40: Therefore, when the owner of the vineyard returns, what will he do to those tenants?”
en.21:41: “He will bring those wretches to a wretched end,” they replied, “and will rent out the vineyard to other tenants who will give him his share of the fruit at harvest time.”
en.21:42: Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in the Scriptures: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?
en.21:43: Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who will produce its fruit.
en.21:44: He who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed.”
en.21:45: When the chief priests and Pharisees heard His parables, they knew that Jesus was speaking about them.
en.21:46: Although they wanted to arrest Him, they were afraid of the crowds, because the people regarded Him as a prophet.

en.12:1: Then Jesus began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a wine vat, and built a watchtower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.
en.12:2: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard.
en.12:3: But they seized the servant, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.
en.12:4: Then he sent them another servant, and they struck him over the head and treated him shamefully.
en.12:5: He sent still another, and this one they killed. He sent many others; some they beat and others they killed.
en.12:6: Finally, having one beloved son, he sent him to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.
en.12:7: But the tenants said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
en.12:8: So they seized the son, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
en.12:9: What then will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and kill those tenants and give the vineyard to others.
en.12:10: Have you never read this Scripture: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
en.12:11: This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”
en.12:12: At this, the leaders sought to arrest Jesus, for they knew that He had spoken this parable against them. But fearing the crowd, they left Him and went away.

en.20:9: Then He proceeded to tell the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard, rented it out to some tenants, and went away for a long time.
en.20:10: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard. But the tenants beat the servant and sent him away empty-handed.
en.20:11: So he sent another servant, but they beat him and treated him shamefully, sending him away empty-handed.
en.20:12: Then he sent a third, but they wounded him and threw him out.
en.20:13: ‘What shall I do?’ asked the owner of the vineyard. ‘I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect him.’
en.20:14: But when the tenants saw the son, they discussed it among themselves and said, ‘This is the heir. Let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
en.20:15: So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What then will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
en.20:16: He will come and kill those tenants and give the vineyard to others.” And when the people heard this, they said, “May such a thing never happen!”
en.20:17: But Jesus looked directly at them and said, “Then what is the meaning of that which is written: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone’?
en.20:18: Everyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed.”
en.20:19: When the scribes and chief priests realized that Jesus had spoken this parable against them, they sought to arrest Him that very hour. But they were afraid of the people.
